headline: North crumbles in floods: 10 pictures reveal nature’s wrath in Himachal, Punjab, Haryana, J-K
content: NEW DELHI: Relentless monsoon rains across Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab and Haryana have killed more than 500 people this season, with fresh landslides, flash floods and collapsing houses claiming dozens of lives in the past two days. Highways remain blocked, rivers are flowing above danger marks, crops have been flattened, and thousands are stranded as the region faces one of its worst weather disasters in decades. Here's 10 pictures reveal nature’s wrath1. Overall death toll crosses 500More than 500 lives have been lost this monsoon across the four northern states. Thousands are stranded as rivers swell and highways remain blocked.2. Himachal Pradesh worst hitHimachal Pradesh has recorded 343 deaths so far. The state continues to battle landslides, flash floods and even fresh snowfall in higher reaches. 3. Sundernagar landslideA massive landslide in Mandi’s Sundernagar killed seven people, including four members of one family. More residents died in similar incidents in Shimla and Kullu, while several bus passengers were injured.4. Road closures in HimachalOver 1,155 roads are still shut, including major routes such as the Chandigarh–Manali highway and the Atal Tunnel approach. Restoration work is hampered by heavy rainfall and a swelling Beas River.5. Snowfall in high passesUnseasonal snowfall in Lahaul-Spiti, Kinnaur and Kullu has stranded trucks at Baralacha Pass (4,890m), cutting off high-altitude areas.6. Jammu & Kashmir crisisSince mid-August, 132 people have died and 33 remain missing. The Jhelum River has crossed the danger mark, reviving fears of 2014 floods. Major rivers including Chenab, Tawi and Ravi are flowing above safe levels.7. Disruptions in J&KThe Vaishno Devi pilgrimage has been suspended. More than 2,000 vehicles are stranded on the Jammu–Srinagar highway due to landslides, while the Railways has cancelled 68 trains from Jammu and Katra until 30 September.8. Punjab declares disasterPunjab has declared the state disaster-affected, facing its worst floods in nearly 40 years. The death toll has risen to 37. More than 1,655 villages in 23 districts have been hit, affecting 3.55 lakh people.9. Crops and farmland destroyed in PunjabOver 1.75 lakh hectares of farmland lie submerged, with Gurdaspur the worst-hit district. Farmers face heavy losses as Bhakra Dam nears its danger level of 1,680 ft.10. Haryana casualties and closuresEight people have died in the state, including three children in Bhiwani after a roof collapse. Two migrant workers were killed in Kurukshetra and three men were electrocuted in Hisar. Schools have been shut in 16 of 22 districts.
